newsitem.title: USA: Boston Scientific drops on earnings forecast.
newsitem.headline: Boston Scientific drops on earnings forecast.

text.p: Shares of Boston Scientific Corp plunged nearly 24 percent after the medical device manufacturer said its first quarter earnings would fall short of analysts' expectations since currency fluctuations hurt revenues.
Several analysts also downgraded the stock.
Boston Scientific dropped 14-1/4 to 46-1/4 and was the most active issue on the New York Stock Exchange at midday on Friday.
Without the impact of changes in exchange rates, net sales for the first quarter increased 27 percent, Boston Scientific said.
"Solid growth was again experienced in both the U.S. and international markets. We continue to work very hard at expanding our global presence," said Boston Scientific Chairman Pete Nicholas.

Several brokerage firms, including Cowen & Co, Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and Salomon Brothers downgraded the stock on Friday. Dillon Read, however, upgraded Boston Scientific to buy from outperform due to the sharp drop in price.

Boston Scientific has spent agressively on infrastructure improvements over the past year, and is suffering from growing pains that will dampen its near-term profitability but enhance its long-term prospects, analysts said.
Boston Scientific "has little room to trip in the near-term with significant volume required to adequately absorb these costs," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell (DMG) said Friday in a research report.

Among Boston Scientific's problems, analysts said, its Medi-Tech division remains below the company's average growth target and emerging markets such as the Far East have not been ramping-up sales as quickly as had been expected.
Longer-term, Boston Scientific remains well-positioned, they said.
"Boston Scientific continues to exhibit robust growth across most of its business," J.P. Morgan said in a research report.
"If management can bring the cost structure back under control, sales growth should start to offset some of these higher costs in the second and third quarter," J.P. Morgan said.
J.P. Morgan trimmed its 1997 earnings estimates to $1.90 a share from $2.12 a share and cut the 1998 estimate to $2.50 a share from $2.80 a share.
Analysts cautioned that investors will have to closely monitor whether Boston Scientific is getting its cost situation under control.
